messages:
Maya: hitting a support case from a customer — they see intermittent 429s and increased latency on redwood-v2-large. Started around 10:12 UTC, correlates with a traffic spike. They say two endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings both affected.
Priya: can you paste the root error payload? 429 or 503? any rate_limit headers?
Maya: 429 with body: `{\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\", \"retry_after\": 1}`. No x-rate-limit headers present. They also saw auth 401 earlier, but that was a separate API key rotation and fixed.
Jonah: did they hit per-account quota or per-model limits? need timestamps + model in the requests. Sometimes SDK retries cause bursts that exceed per-model RPM/TPM even if overall account seeming under quota.
Maya: sending sample timeline and one anonymized request log. Sequence: 10:12:01 -> 30 concurrent /generate, 10:12:05 -> SDK client retry round, 10:12:06 -> 120 embeddings calls in 10s.
Alex: that last bit smells like concurrency + burst. redwood-v2-large has documented per-model rate of ~120 RPM and 600 TPM (example). If many short requests come in and SDK retries, token-based TPM can blow out quickly.
Priya: customer says they have a billing hold event around 10:15 (billing-bot flagged a declined payment for a backup card). If billing triggers account throttling, we return 402 or reduced throughput — but they reported only 429s, not 402. Could be separate.
Maya: repro attempt: I ran curl loop against redwood-v2-large with 1-token prompts, 150 req/s for 30s. I saw server respond 429 after ~8s. Logs show `quota.exhausted.model` in infra logs.
Jonah: good repro. Two things to confirm: (1) per-model RPM/TPM enforcement vs per-account. (2) concurrency limits — max active sessions per model might queue or reject.
Alex: infra-bot, please pull the model-limit table for redwood-v2-large for this org id org_9x*.
infra-bot: fetched limits for org_9x*: model=redwood-v2-large, per_min_rpm=180, per_min_tpm=650, max_concurrency=40, context_max_tokens=8192. Also current burst window shows 1.6x above rolling RPM at incident start.
Priya: max_concurrency=40 — their spike had ~120 concurrent short calls for generate + embeddings, so concurrency alone explains rejects. When concurrency exceeded we can either queue (if capacity) or fast-fail with 429. Looks like fast-fail mode for that pool.
Maya: customer confused because their global usage is < account quota. How to explain?
Jonah: explain per-model limits and per-pool behavior: even if account-wide quota fine, a single hot model can exhaust its pool. Also small prompts => high TPM; embeddings are token-heavy if batch/context large.
Maya: they also mentioned long-context requests (40k tokens) earlier in the day that coincided with higher latency. Could large context evict other KV caches and reduce throughput?
Alex: yes — long context increases per-request GPU memory and can reduce effective concurrency. We auto-route long-context to larger instances which have lower parallelism. If those instances are scarce, other model requests share degraded capacity -> increased latency and 429s.
Priya: suggested mitigation steps to customer: (1) spread requests with client-side pacing (token bucket), (2) add jitter to retries, (3) use batching for embeddings, (4) pin to a model variant with higher concurrency or request Dedicated capacity.
Maya: shared a repro snippet to customer for client-side pacing: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do
  sleep $(python -c 'import random; print(random.random()*0.02)')
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-large","input":"hi"}' &
done
wait
```
Jonah: also recommended checking SDK version — we had a bug where exponential backoff defaulted to 200ms base causing thundering retries; fixed in 0.12.3.
Maya: customer also curious about headers to look for on 429s. What should they check?
Alex: we set `x-rw-retry-after-ms` when available, and `x-rw-quota-type: model|account`. If missing, recommend looking up request-id and send to support.
Priya: for billing-related throttles, billing-bot: flagged `invoice.failed` at 10:15 for org_9x* but no auto-throttle for that threshold. I confirmed no account-level suspension.
Maya: next steps I will: (1) send them the infra-bot limits screenshot, (2) provide pacing + SDK upgrade + jitter guidance, (3) offer a Dedicated trial for predictable throughput.
Jonah: open a follow-up to product for clearer docs on per-model vs account quotas — several customers keep getting tripped by that difference.
Maya: thanks all. I'll update the case and mark for a SRE handoff if they repro on our end after changes. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: note created INC-2026-487 for invoice.fail org_9x* (auto).
